saints.name: St. Leo the Great
saints.title: Pope and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The pope whose Tome guided the Council of Chalcedon and who turned back Attila from the gates of Rome…
biography: Leo became Bishop of Rome in 440 and governed the Church through a time of doctrinal strife and barbarian invasion. His dogmatic letter, the Tome of Leo, set forth the true faith of the two natures in the one person of Christ and was acclaimed by the Council of Chalcedon in 451 as the voice of Peter.

In 452 he went out to meet Attila the Hun and persuaded him to spare Rome, and later interceded with the Vandals who sacked the city. A vigorous defender of the primacy of the Roman See and a great preacher, he died on 10 November 461 and was later declared a Doctor of the Church.
saints.knownFor: The Tome of Leo and the defence of the faith at Chalcedon.

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; Doctor of the Church (1754)

sources.text: Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), “Pope St. Leo I (the Great)”
